failure_summary.description: Answers included unnecessary formal, generic-type, or ordinal words instead of the clue’s shorter conventional name or title.
Selected a related structure mentioned in context rather than the specific structure requested by the clue.
The bare-work-title heuristic favors a creator even when the clue and context point to the work’s source or inspiration.

patch.reasoning: Sharpen the existing granularity guidance so identifying details are not carried into answers unless requested or integral to the conventional name. Revise the bare-work-title rule to infer the intended relation rather than defaulting to a creator. The structure-versus-related-object error is already covered by existing slot and evidence rules.

edits.target: - Use the context-supported conventional form of a name or answer, and include additional name parts only when needed to distinguish otherwise-confusable entities.
edits.content: - Use the shortest conventional name at the clue’s requested level. Do not mechanically expand a recognized short name to a formal full name, add a generic type word, or carry an ordinal or other identifying modifier into the answer unless it is integral to the conventional name, explicitly requested, or needed to distinguish entities.

edits.target: - If a prompt consists only of a work title and year, do not answer with its generic type (such as “film”). Look for a principal person explicitly and centrally associated with that work in the context, such as its director, author, or creator, and answer with that person only when the association is clear. If the context offers no clear intended relation, treat the prompt as underdetermined rather than guessing.
edits.content: - For a terse work-title clue, do not answer with the work’s generic type or assume that the creator is wanted. Use the wording and context to infer the intended relation: if the clue frames a work as an adaptation, retelling, or remake and points to its source, return that source work; return a creator only when that relation is clearly intended. If no intended relation is supported, treat the prompt as underdetermined rather than guessing.
